title: Profile-guided quant routing: case study and microbenchmarks
content:
Summary:

This is a working notebook for a small experimental push: build a lightweight profile-guided router that dispatches incoming requests to the best-fitting quantized kernel/model variant at request time. The idea: instead of globally exposing N quantized variants and choosing by static policy (model size / region / SLAs), use a 2-step fast profile on the request prefix to predict which quant variant will meet a latency SLO with minimal quality loss.

Why this exploration: we often see wide variance in per-request cost and quality sensitivity. Some prompts are robust to aggressive quant; others show disproportionate quality degradation. If we can cheaply predict that sensitivity and pick kernel+quantization accordingly, we can recover tail latency without blanket conservative choices. This doc captures the prototype, microbenchmarks, and open questions.

Hypothesis:
- A 20-30ms micro-profile (first N tokens + cheap feature extraction) can predict which quant variant will exceed p95 latency under current load with useful precision (>70% precision).
- Routing to quant-aggressive kernels when safe reduces p95 by 10-25% and cost by ~12% with <2% average quality regression on our MCQA and log-prob metrics.

Experiment setup:
- Hardware: 1x A100-40GB (nv_peer_mem), 1x H100-80GB (for cross-device comparison), testbed is isolated with no other tenants.
- Models: Llama-2-13B (fp16 baseline), Llama-2-13B-GPTQ (4-bit GPTQ variant), Llama-2-13B-AWQ (AWQ per-layer config), and int8-packed custom kernel variant (fused-gemm-int8-packed).
- Kernel builds: stock fused-matmul (baseline), fused-gemm-int8-packed (our tiled int8 kernel), awq-opset-3 (AWQ optimized ops), gptq-packed-kernel-v2.
- Toolchain: internal quant lib + offline GPTQ scripts (git PR 4123), AWQ conversions via awq-convert (modified).
- Dataset: 800 prompts sampled from production anonymized request logs (mixed short Q/A, long instructions, code snippets). Held-out 200 prompts for validation. Also evaluated MCQA accuracy on TriviaQA subset (50 items) as a surrogate for semantic degradation.

Profile-guided router prototype:
- Step 0: cheap tokenizer-based features: prefix length, fraction of numeric/tokens, average token id entropy (via small 64-d LM probe), presence of code tokens, and prompt complexity score (heuristic). Extraction cost: ~15-40ms depending on prefix length.
- Step 1: lightweight predictor (XGBoost micro model) trained to predict whether aggressive-quant variant will keep log-prob delta < threshold and satisfy p95 latency < SLO (SLO=450ms).
- Step 2: route to selected variant and kernel; fallback to baseline when predictor uncertain.

Microbenchmark results (single-A100, cold-warm steady-state):
- Baseline fp16 p50/p95 latency (13B): 82ms / 512ms, tokens/sec: 2300
- GPTQ-4bit (gptq-packed-kernel-v2): p50/p95: 74ms / 420ms, tokens/sec: 2600, avg log-prob delta vs fp16: -0.032 nats/token, MCQA accuracy delta: -1.8 pp
- AWQ (awq-opset-3): p50/p95: 70ms / 460ms, tokens/sec: 2720, avg log-prob delta: -0.045 nats/token, MCQA delta: -2.6 pp
- Int8-packed kernel (fused-gemm-int8-packed): p50/p95: 60ms / 380ms, tokens/sec: 2950, avg log-prob delta: -0.055 nats/token, MCQA delta: -3.5 pp

Note: p95 is highly dependent on sequence shape; the int8-packed kernel improves tail significantly for short token-step workloads but shows occasional jitter for long-code prompts (see anomaly section).

Profile predictor performance (validation set):
- Predict 'safe-to-route-to-int8' precision: 72%, recall: 68% (threshold tuned for precision).
- Predict 'safe-to-route-to-gptq' precision: 79%, recall: 74%
- Prediction latency (features + model): median 28ms (95th 45ms).

End-to-end routing simulation (synthetic load generator replaying 10k requests at 70% of baseline capacity):
- Static conservative policy (route 20% to fp16, 40% to GPTQ, 40% to AWQ): overall p95 420ms, average cost baseline 1.00x
- Profile-guided router (thresholding + uncertainty fallback): overall p95 360ms (-14% vs static), average cost 0.88x (-12%), MCQA delta vs baseline fp16: -2.3 pp average (within SLO for these customers).

Failure modes and anomalies observed:
- Long code-generating prompts: int8-packed kernel sometimes produces severe token hallucination patterns on specific layer types; manifests as large log-prob swings after certain tokens. Replicate: prompt containing inline Python triple backticks + long example inputs.
- Cache invalidation: routing introduces a new cache dimension (variant), increasing KV cache miss rate by ~4% (we simulated cache-isolated vs shared routing). Effective token cost can increase if cache fragmentation isn't handled.
- Micro-profile overhead: for very short prompts (<8 tokens) profiling overhead outweighs gains. We should disable routing for that bucket.

Practical recommendations so far:
- Disable profile-guided routing for requests with prefix length <12 tokens.
- Add lightweight per-variant KV cache warming heuristics: when routing toggles variant for a request, issue a background masked warmup request to pre-populate KV for subsequent tokens (cheap and amortizable).
- Use a conservative uncertainty threshold to limit false positives routing to int8; prefer routing to GPTQ as middle ground when ambiguous.
- Augment predictor with a small online feedback signal: if selected variant shows log-prob drop beyond expected, mark variant as suspect and temporarily revert.

Open questions / next steps:
- Re-run on multi-tenant noisy host to quantify predictor robustness under interference; current tests are single-tenant.
- Investigate long-code prompt failure in int8-packed kernel: instrument per-layer activations and compare AWQ/GPTQ differences; open a tracking ticket.
- Explore a hybrid caching strategy: store shared KV for fp16/GPTQ and light ephemeral KV for aggressive int8 to reduce fragmentation.
- Consider deploying a 'shadow' routing mode in production where routing decisions are logged but not enacted, to collect distribution shift and calibrate thresholds.

Action items:
- Ravi: open debug PR to dump per-layer quant activation stats for failing code prompts (JIRA-INF-3012).
- Priya: run multi-tenant replay on staging cluster (H100) and collect p95 deltas (due 2026-10-12).
- Ethan: prototype background KV warmups and measure overhead (POC branch runtime/kv-warmup).
- Sofia: refine predictor features (add simple syntactic parse features) and retrain on larger corpus; measure precision target >80%.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could try an alternative cheap probe: run a 1-step fp16 generation for 1 token and measure model-internal variance; may be more predictive than token-entropy heuristics but costlier.
- For some customers we can expose a per-route quant-policy toggle (explicit opt-in) instead of auto-routing.

Attachments / sketches: expectation to add exported CSV with per-prompt deltas, profiler flame samples, and a short replay script used for simulations (will upload to linked PR).

Unresolved:
- Is the micro-profile cost amortizable across heavy concurrency scenarios? Need multi-tenant experiments.
- How to set SLAs per-customer when profile-guided routing changes tail shapes?

End of notebook. This is intentionally rough; aiming to capture the prototype, early numbers, and the immediate next work. If this looks useful we should branch a follow-up RFC to discuss operational guardrails and rollout plan.
